diagram_name: Hardware Finding to Setup Branch Matcher
learning_objective: The learner will apply the hardware-to-setup rules of this chapter to 6 findings by choosing the setup branch each finding triggers, with at least 5 of 6 correct.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** hardware-branch-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** apply
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply the hardware-to-setup rules of this chapter to 6 findings by choosing the setup branch each finding triggers, with at least 5 of 6 correct. **Prerequisites:** CPU architecture, x86_64, aarch64, dedicated GPU memory, unified memory, multi-GPU system, NVIDIA driver, CUDA (all defined in the sections above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of the 6 findings the learner commits one branch from the six listed in Content before the sim reveals the answer. A choice is correct when it equals the Correct branch column. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the finding text is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Every DGX has dedicated GPU memory. (2) A download that completes will run on any DGX. (3) `nvidia-smi` always reports how much GPU memory there is. (4) A newer CUDA build is always better. **Instructional Rationale:** Apply-level work needs the learner to use a rule on a new case, so each finding is a realistic probe result that triggers exactly one branch. Committing before the reveal separates a reasoned choice from recognition. **Content:** The six setup branches the learner chooses from are: "Use aarch64 packages", "Use x86_64 packages", "Size models against one shared memory pool", "Size models against one GPU's dedicated memory", "Plan to split the model across several GPUs", and "Choose a CUDA build at or below the driver's version". | # | Finding shown to the learner | Correct branch | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `uname -m` prints `aarch64`. | Use aarch64 packages | The processor is Arm, so only builds for aarch64 will run. | | 2 | `uname -m` prints `x86_64`. | Use x86_64 packages | The processor is Intel or AMD, so builds for x86_64 are the ones that run. | | 3 | `nvidia-smi` lists one GPU with memory reported as `Not Supported`; `free -h` shows about 120 GiB of memory. | Size models against one shared memory pool | The GPU has no memory of its own, so the system's memory is the limit. | | 4 | `nvidia-smi` lists one GPU with 80 GB of memory; `free -h` shows 512 GiB. | Size models against one GPU's dedicated memory | The weights must fit in the GPU's own 80 GB, however much system RAM there is. | | 5 | `nvidia-smi` lists eight GPUs of 80 GB each. | Plan to split the model across several GPUs | A model larger than 80 GB can run only if it is divided across the GPUs. | | 6 | The driver reports CUDA 13.0; the framework build you downloaded needs CUDA 13.2. | Choose a CUDA build at or below the driver's version | The driver sets a ceiling, and a runtime above it will not start. | **Provenance:** The findings are synthetic examples written for this exercise, and the sim labels them "synthetic example". The meanings of the branches come from the sections of this chapter above. **Rules:** Findings are shown in the fixed order 1 to 6. Each finding allows exactly one branch choice, and the choice is final. A finding is correct only when the chosen branch equals the Correct branch. Each finding triggers exactly one branch of the six. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads finding 1. 2. The learner chooses one of the six branches and confirms. 3. The sim shows the correct branch and the Why text, and marks the finding correct or incorrect. 4. The learner repeats for findings 2 to 6. After finding 6 the sim shows the score and, for each miss, the misconception behind it. **Feedback:** Six findings, fixed order, one confirmed choice each, no second attempt. Correct: "Correct" followed by the Why text. Incorrect: "Not quite" followed by the correct branch and the Why text. The final score reads "n of 6 correct". **Starting State:** Finding 1 is shown with no branch chosen, and the question on screen is "Which setup branch does this finding trigger?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter states that aarch64 and x86_64 builds are not interchangeable, that on unified memory the GPU has no memory of its own and `nvidia-smi` reports it as `Not Supported`, that a model larger than one GPU's dedicated memory must be split across GPUs, and that the driver sets a ceiling on the CUDA version.
